capability: Apps: the apps a store installs and manages in its admin (Shopify Apps, Apps and channels; Salla My apps, Installed apps / التطبيقات المثبتة)
note: Parent of CM-APP-002 to CM-APP-009. Both platforms keep a store's apps as one admin place: Shopify's Apps section, its apps routes and the staff permissions APPLICATIONS and LIMITED_APPLICATIONS (SH-S-1495, SH-S-5028); Salla's dashboard app @salla.sa/ui-merchant-apps at /apps, with My apps at /apps/installed and the permission marketplace_apps_management (SA-S-3541, SA-S-1883, SA-S-2629). Their groupings put the rest under apps: Shopify's Apps section holds App development (SH-S-7143), its Apps and channels permissions hold Approve app charges (SH-I-1008), its help center's apps manual holds Finding and choosing apps and App extensions and functions (SH-I-2101, SH-I-2104), and an app contains its functions (SH-S-0682); Salla's /apps holds the App Store and My apps (SA-S-1884, SA-S-1883), and its App API holds an app's Subscriptions and Settings (SA-S-1077, SA-S-1076). Homonym (notes): Salla's app maker (App Maker, app builder, تطبيق خاص بمتجرك, the publishing policy for Google's and Apple's app stores) is the store's own mobile shopping app, domain E, not an app in this sense.

capability: App store: the platform's marketplace of apps, with its categories and its review of the apps it lists (Shopify App Store, App distribution; Salla App Store, متجر تطبيقات سلة)
note: Shopify's App Store is its own (shopify.com's header navigation, SH-S-2753), reviewed by Shopify (SH-S-0698); Salla's App Store is a dashboard link (/apps, SA-S-1884), and Salla's team reviews, accepts or rejects apps (SA-S-0023). The store's terms for listed apps are here (Salla's App Store policy, SA-C-175); its rule that listed apps bill through the platform is in CM-APP-003. App distribution (Shopify's choice between the App Store and custom distribution, SH-S-2852, SH-S-0692) is here; custom distribution is cited in CM-APP-009.

capability: App charges billed through the platform: the platform bills the merchant for an app and keeps a share for itself (Shopify app charges, Shopify App Pricing, Billing; Salla App Subscriptions, payment through Salla / العمولات والدفع)
note: M-010 is a difference of grain: Shopify keeps app charges (SH-C-019) apart from partner payouts (SH-C-169), and Salla keeps both in SA-C-195. This capability is the charge: billed on the platform's own invoice or through the platform, with the platform's share. The payout of the developer's share, as a partner's finances (Shopify's SH-C-169; Salla's Payouts, Billings, Operation records and Billing System Salla partners), is left to area PTN, which a later batch of this part takes (notes).

capability: App lifecycle events: the platform notifies an app when it is installed, uninstalled, authorized or updated, and when its trial or subscription changes (Shopify app/uninstalled, app_subscriptions/update, App Events API; Salla App Events)
note: Both platforms name the events by the app's lifecycle in a store (Shopify app/uninstalled and app_subscriptions/update, SH-S-1153, SH-S-1156; Salla app.installed, app.uninstalled, app.subscription.started, SA-S-1649, SA-S-1569, SA-S-1572). Both also place app events on the partner's side: Salla's App Events are partner portal events (SA-S-5093), and Shopify's App Events API is in its Partner API (SH-I-0075, in SH-C-168, area PTN). I put the capability under apps, which its events are about, and not under the partner programme, whose capability doesn't exist yet in this part (notes).

capability: Functions: app-written functions that the platform hosts and calls itself, within its own processing or on a store's events (Shopify Functions; Salla App Functions)
note: M-070, one to one. Shopify's functions customize its backend logic and Shopify invokes them within the customer journey, never by URL (SH-S-0681, SH-S-0683); Salla's run when events occur in a store, fully managed by Salla, some of them synchronous and blocking (SA-S-0187, SA-S-0190, SA-S-0189). The function APIs for single features (Shopify's discount, delivery, payment and validation functions) are in the domains of what they customize (C and D, under also); this capability is functions as such.

capability: App UI in the admin: an app's own pages and extensions inside the merchant's admin (Shopify App Home, Admin UI extensions, Polaris; Salla Embedded SDK)
note: Parent of CM-APP-007 and CM-APP-008. Shopify keeps both forms in one concern (SH-C-164: Admin action, Admin block, App home, Admin link, Polaris), so it lands here; Salla's Embedded SDK (SA-C-197) is the iframe form only, so it lands in CM-APP-007. Other surfaces for apps' UI (checkout, customer accounts, POS, the theme) are in the domains of those surfaces.

capability: Embedded app page: an app's own page shown inside the admin, in an iframe or as an extension (Shopify App Home; Salla embedded app pages, Embedded SDK)
note: Joined on role (a reading): Shopify's App Home, its app_home target and its App Home (iframe) API (SH-S-2182, SH-I-0054), and Salla's third-party application running in an iframe in the Merchant Dashboard through the Embedded SDK, with the dashboard's /embedded and /{app-name} apps (SA-S-0197, SA-S-3585, SA-S-3581). Neither side defines the other's term.

capability: Admin UI extensions: an app's blocks, actions, print actions and links on the admin's own pages (Shopify Admin UI extensions: admin_block, admin_action, admin_print, admin_link)
note: Shopify only so far: extension targets that put an app's functionality on core admin pages (SH-S-0711), such as admin.product-details.block.render. Salla's statements hold none found (its cell); its released flag apps-iframe-sections (SA-S-3427) doesn't say where the sections show, so it is cited in the parent.

capability: Custom apps: apps a store develops, or has developed, for itself, not listed in the app store (Shopify custom apps, App development, custom distribution)
note: Shopify only so far: the admin's App development, in its Apps section, with its staff permissions and a plan line (SH-S-7143, SH-S-5038, SH-S-7054), and custom distribution for a specific merchant (SH-S-0693). Salla's statements hold none found (its cell).

capability: App settings: parameters an app's developer defines for the app, held by the platform for each store and read through its API (Salla App Settings, the App API's Settings)
note: Salla only so far: Shopify's statements hold none found. Under CM-APP-001: Salla's App API holds Settings beside Subscriptions (CM-APP-003), and its App Events include app.settings.updated (CM-APP-004). Not an app's page in the admin (CM-APP-007): U-048 apart.

capability: Developer API: the platform's API through which apps read and write a store's data and receive its events, with the conventions common to it (Shopify GraphQL Admin API, REST Admin API (legacy), API usage; Salla Merchant API)
note: Parent of CM-API-002 to CM-API-011. Both platforms list authorization, scopes, rate limits, versioning and webhooks as entries of one list of API resources (Shopify's api-resources: API authentication, Access scopes, Limits, Versioning, Bulk operations, Webhooks; Salla's docs under one folder, 841847: Authorization, Rate Limiting, Versioning, Change Log, Webhooks, Conditional Webhooks). M-073 is a difference of grain: Shopify's SH-C-171 holds the conventions together, so it lands here; Salla's SA-C-201 and SA-C-202 land in CM-API-005 and CM-API-006.

capability: App authorization: how an app is authorized by the merchant to call the API for a store (Shopify API authentication; Salla Authorization, Salla OAuth 2.0)
note: U-046 joined here. Shopify's side is held only as an inventory entry (SH-I-0030); its admin grant routes (app/grant, oauth/request_grant) are SH-C-156's, cited in CM-APP-001.

capability: Access scopes: the parts of a store's data an app may read or write, which the merchant grants (Shopify access scopes; Salla App Scope)
note: M-068. Shopify's scopes that need its approval (SH-C-159) land here, finer than it, with no capability of their own.

capability: Protected customer data: an app's access to buyers' personal data, which the platform approves and bounds (Shopify protected customer data, Level 2 access, read_customer_email)
note: Shopify only so far. Under access scopes: Shopify lists Protected customer data permissions and its read_customer_* scopes among its access scopes (SH-I-2428, SH-I-2472).

capability: API rate limits: how many requests an app may make, and what happens when it exceeds them (Shopify API rate limits, Limits, leaky bucket; Salla Rate Limiting)
note: M-073. Both platforms vary the limits by the store's plan.

capability: API versioning and change log: the platform's versions of its API, when it adds one, and its record of changes (Shopify Versioning; Salla Versioning, Change Log)
note: M-073. Shopify's statements hold no change log found.

capability: Bulk operations: the platform's API for operations over a store's data in bulk, with a webhook topic when one finishes (Shopify Bulk operations, bulk_operations/finish)
note: Shopify only so far.

capability: Webhooks: subscriptions through which the platform sends a store's events to an app's or another service's address (Shopify Webhooks, webhook topics; Salla Webhooks)
note: M-069. Parent of CM-API-009 to CM-API-011. The topics on an app's own lifecycle are CM-APP-004's.

capability: Webhooks set up in the admin: the merchant subscribes an address to the store's events from the admin, without an app (Shopify Settings > Notifications > Webhooks; Salla Developer tools, إرسال الإخطارات لخدمات أخرى عبر Webhooks)
note: Both platforms give it an admin route: Shopify notification-settings:webhooks, Salla /manage/webhooks. Salla gates it by plan.

capability: Conditional webhooks (Salla Conditional Webhooks)
note: Salla only so far, and only by its title: a page of its own in Salla's API documentation list, whose definition the concern map doesn't hold.

capability: Privacy compliance webhooks: topics through which the platform passes data subject requests and erasure to an app, which it must answer (Shopify mandatory compliance webhooks: customers/data_request, customers/redact, shop/redact)
note: Shopify only so far.

capability: Developer tools and documentation: the platform's own tools and docs for building apps and themes (Shopify.dev: Dev docs, CLI, and more; Salla Dev Tools: Partners Agent Kit, Salla Apps Playbook, Salla CLI)
note: Parent of CM-DVT-002. Salla's developer docs have a top-level menu Dev Tools whose children are Partners Agent Kit, Salla Apps Playbook and Salla CLI (SA-S-1176 to SA-S-1179); Shopify's product list names Shopify.dev, "Dev docs, CLI, and more" (SH-I-1990, an inventory entry of SH-C-171). Partners Agent Kit and the Apps Playbook are held only as folder titles, with no definition, so they stay in the parent, not capabilities of their own (my judgment). Not under CM-API-001: Salla's Dev Tools is a menu of its own, not an entry of the API's folder 841847, and Shopify's CLI is in its API resources list only as an unplaced entry (SH-I-0039), which a cell can't cite. Citing SH-I-1990 here and in CM-DVT-002 makes SH-C-171 (landed in CM-API-001) strained, and batch 2's U-047 row for (SH-C-171, SA-C-203) no longer holds (notes, batch 3).

capability: Command-line tool: the platform's CLI for creating and working on apps and themes (Shopify CLI, in Shopify.dev; Salla CLI, Apps Command, Twilight Themes Command)
note: Salla gives it a docs folder of its own, under Dev Tools (SA-S-1179), with its commands as folders of its docs (SA-S-1106, SA-S-1107, SA-S-1109). Shopify's side is only the words "CLI" in the entry Shopify.dev (SH-I-1990); its API resources entry Shopify CLI (SH-I-0039) is unplaced, so not cited.

capability: Partner stores: the stores a partner keeps in its partner dashboard, to build and test on or to prepare for merchants (Shopify Partner Dashboard Stores; Salla Partners portal Stores: Demo Stores, Ready Stores)
note: Parent of CM-DVT-004 and CM-DVT-005. Salla's Partners portal has a menu item Stores (position 27) whose children are Demo Stores, Ready Stores and Store management (SA-S-1931, SA-S-1932, SA-S-1933: each "parent": 27); Shopify's Partner Dashboard has an item Stores (SH-I-2086). The item Stores itself (SA-S-1930) is placed in no concern, so not cited. Store management is SA-C-013's (domain A, partner access to a merchant's store), not cited. Joined on role: neither side defines the other's term (notes).

capability: Development stores: free stores the platform gives developers to build and test apps and themes before launch (Shopify development store; Salla Demo Stores, المتاجر التجريبية, devstore)
note: Salla's place: the Partners portal link Demo Stores, /demo-stores, and the dashboard app @salla.sa/ui-merchant-devstore at /store-dev. Shopify names "the development store" only in a theme tool's guide (SH-C-158/boundary/SH-S-6300); no place of its own is held.

capability: Ready stores: stores a partner prepares and publishes for merchants, each reviewed by the platform before it is published (Salla Ready Stores, المتاجر الجاهزة)
note: Salla's place: the Partners portal link Ready Stores, /store (SA-S-1932). What a ready store holds, and who buys it, isn't stated beyond its review (SA-S-5111).

capability: Partner programme: the platform's programme for the developers, agencies and marketers who work with its merchants, with its terms and the dashboard where a partner works (Shopify Partner Program, Shopify Partners, Partner Dashboard, Partner Terms of Service; Salla Partners, منصة شركاء سلة, Partners portal, Developer Portal, سياسة الانضمام إلى برنامج شركاء سلة)
note: Parent of CM-PTN-002 to CM-PTN-009. Both platforms keep a partner's work in one dashboard and under one agreement: Shopify's Partner Dashboard (Home, Stores, Payouts, Organization, Partner settings, Dev dashboard: SH-I-2085 to SH-I-2094) and its Partner Program Agreement; Salla's Partners portal (its navigation holds Dashboard, My Services, Affiliates, Influencer, Payments, Employees, Settings: SA-S-1905 to SA-S-1947) and its policy for joining the programme. M-071 is a difference of grain: Shopify's SH-C-168 holds the programme, its terms, the dashboard and the Partner API; Salla splits the partner account (SA-C-204), the contract (SA-C-176) and app events (SA-C-193, in CM-APP-004). The Partner API (SH-S-0838) is cited here; the seed and Shopify's API resources list put it beside the platform's other APIs, so the coordinator may want a child of CM-API-001 for it (notes).

capability: Partner account: the partner's account or organization, with its eligibility, its identity verification, its settings and its employees (Shopify Partner Account, Partner organization, Organization, Partner settings; Salla Personal Identity, Verified, Employees, Settings)
note: Places of its own: Shopify's Partner Dashboard items Organization and Partner settings and the Partner API object Organization; Salla's Partners portal links Employees and Settings and its lists of identity types and statuses. Identity verification and employees are kept here, not as capabilities of their own: only Salla shows either, and both are parts of the partner's account in its portal (my judgment).

capability: Partner payouts: the platform pays a partner what it owes, such as its share of app revenue and its commissions, on a schedule and subject to holds (Shopify Payouts, partner-payouts, Transactions; Salla Payouts, مستحقات المطورين)
note: Both put it in the partner's dashboard: Shopify's Partner Dashboard item Payouts and its organization settings route partner-payouts; Salla's Partners portal link Payouts under Payments. M-010 is a difference of grain: Shopify's SH-C-169 is payouts alone, landed here by the term Payouts; Salla's SA-C-195 holds app charges and payouts, landed in CM-APP-003 by batch 1, its payout statements cited here.

capability: Partner billing: the platform invoices the partner, who sees and pays the invoices in its dashboard (Shopify partner-billing; Salla Billings, Billing System Salla partners, Operation records)
note: Places of its own: Shopify's organization settings route partner-billing, with the same eligibility as partner-payouts (SH-S-5241); Salla's Partners portal links Billings and Operation records under Payments and its docs link Billing System Salla partners. What the invoices charge the partner for isn't stated on either platform (batch 1's gap).

capability: Partner services for merchants: a directory or marketplace through which merchants find and hire partners' services, and partners list and deliver them (Shopify Partner Directory, Expert services fees, Schedule intro call, Bring your own partner; Salla Merchant Services, experts, Services, Orders Center, Service Provider Portfolio)
note: Parent of CM-PTN-006 and CM-PTN-007. Under the partner programme by the grouping both share on the partner's side: Shopify's Partner Directory is set by the Partner Program Agreement (SH-S-0760, partners/terms); Salla's My Services (Services, Orders Center, Service Provider Portfolio) is in the Partners portal. The merchant's side is in each admin: Shopify's plan subscription routes in Billing; Salla's dashboard link Merchant Services at /manage/experts. U-066 joined here.

capability: Agency store-growth programme: the platform assigns a merchant's store, with the merchant's prior consent, to an accredited partner agency, which activates and develops it (Salla اتفاقية الوكالات لتقديم خدمات لتجار سلة, برنامج تسريع نمو المتاجر)
note: Salla's place: its own agreement on partners.salla.com (SA-S-5124). A finer part of partner services for merchants: here the platform assigns the store, rather than the merchant choosing the partner.

capability: Global selling programme for partners: the platform connects partners with merchants expanding abroad, whom they serve with payments, merchant-of-record and other services (Salla global-selling-program, المدفوعات و البيع بالنيابة (MoR))
note: Salla's place: its own page on partners.salla.com (SA-S-5128). Kept apart from Shopify's Managed Markets (SH-C-110, domain E), which Q1 left unclear (U-076): Salla's is a programme for partners, not the platform selling on the merchant's behalf.

capability: Referral programme for the platform's plans: a member earns a commission on sales of the platform's plans it brings, under the programme's terms (Salla برنامج الإحالة لباقات سلة, اتفاقية استخدام التسويق بالعمولة)
note: Salla's place: its own agreement, on salla.com and partners.salla.com (SA-S-2210; SA-S-0019, from partners.salla.com/legal/privacy-affiliate), and a help article. Under the partner programme: the agreement is one of the Partners portal's legal pages, and its terms address "the partner member of the programme" (SA-I-2619). Its earnings are paid to the merchant's wallet (SA-S-5077), so a member can be a merchant (a reading). The same agreement holds the commission clause cited in CM-PTN-009 (SA-S-0043, under SA-C-206's key).

capability: Partner affiliates and influencers: partners take up affiliate opportunities and influencer campaigns in the partner dashboard and earn commissions on the orders they bring (Salla Affiliates, Affiliate Marketplace, Affiliate Orders, Influencer, Campaign Orders, Marketing Tools)
note: Salla's place: the Partners portal menus Affiliates, Influencer and Marketing Tools (SA-S-1915 to SA-S-1925), with the merchant's side in the dashboard app @salla.sa/ui-merchant-partner-marketing. Shopify's nearest statements are Shopify Collabs (SH-C-134) and the App Store category Affiliate program apps (SH-C-194), which scope.tsv gives domain D without F under also: not cited here, and U-056 rules both pairs apart (notes).

capability: Workflow automation: automations the merchant builds from triggers and actions, within the store and across its apps (Shopify Flow, Workflow Automation)
note: Only Shopify shows it so far: Shopify Flow, "a free ecommerce automation platform that enables you to automate tasks and processes within your Shopify store and across your apps" (SH-S-0752), with the staff permissions View, create, and delete automations and Manage connections and secrets (category AUTOMATIONS, SH-S-7161, SH-S-7162), the extension targets Flow trigger, Flow action and Flow template for apps (SH-S-2242, SH-S-2240), and the App Store category Workflow automation apps (SH-I-1950). Salla's automatic order features (Auto tags, Auto assignment) and its Conditional Webhooks, the seed's leads for this area, are single features of other capabilities, not a tool for building automations (notes). Homonym risk: Shopify's Create marketing automations (SH-C-129, domain D) is marketing's own, not this.

capability: AI tools for merchants: the platform's AI features in the merchant's admin (Shopify AI-powered tools, AI features in the Shopify admin; Salla AI tools for merchants)
note: Parent of CM-AIA-002 to CM-AIA-004, a grain I chose (notes): Shopify's help center keeps Sidekick and Shopify Magic in one manual section, ai-powered-tools (SH-S-0736's page; SH-S-7488, AI features in the Shopify admin, is on its page shopify-magic), and Salla's one concern SA-C-012 holds its AI Connector, its AI agent app and its AI generators together. No Salla statement groups them: its features are flags and settings, each on its own (a gap).

capability: AI assistant in the admin: an AI agent the merchant works with inside the admin (Shopify Sidekick, AI assistant for commerce; Salla AI agent, @salla.sa/ui-merchant-ai-agent, merchant-multi-agent-assistant)
note: Joined on role, a reading (notes): Sidekick is "an AI-enabled commerce assistant in your Shopify admin" (SH-S-0736); Salla's dashboard app @salla.sa/ui-merchant-ai-agent at /ai-agent (SA-S-3577) and its unreleased flag merchant-multi-agent-assistant (SA-S-3187) are named for an AI agent and assistant for the merchant, never defined. Homonym: Shopify's "commerce agents" (SH-S-0714) act on behalf of buyers, in CM-AIA-005, not this.

capability: AI content generation: text the platform's AI writes for the merchant, such as product descriptions, blog posts and SEO fields (Shopify Magic; Salla ai-description-generator, ai-seo-generator, توليد تحسينات SEO عبر الذكاء الاصطناعي)
note: Shopify Magic generates product descriptions and blog posts in the product and article editors (SH-S-7203, SH-S-7204, SH-S-7206, SH-S-7207); Salla's flags ai-description-generator and ai-seo-generator are unreleased (SA-S-3488, SA-S-3489), and its plan line generates SEO improvements with AI for an extra fee (SA-S-2133, plan سلة برو). Salla's SEO plan line and ai-seo-generator are also statements of SA-C-033 (SEO, domain E); the cells cite SA-C-012's keys.

capability: AI connector: linking an outside AI assistant to the store through an MCP server the platform provides (Salla AI Connector, salla-mcp)
note: Only Salla shows it so far: the setting Salla AI Connector (general/salla-mcp, SA-S-1725), whose ChatGPT step lets the merchant add a custom MCP server from Salla (SA-S-5005), and the released flag salla-mcp (SA-S-3188). Who the connected assistant acts for is not stated. Under CM-AIA-001 because its setting is in the merchant's own settings (a reading). Kept apart from Shopify's UCP-compliant MCP servers, which serve agents acting on behalf of buyers (SH-S-0714, CM-AIA-005): the shared term MCP doesn't show the same object (notes). Q1's M-079 joins it with WooCommerce MCP.

capability: Agentic commerce: buyers discovering and buying a store's products through AI chats and agents, on channels the platform or third parties operate (Shopify Agentic Storefronts, Sell in AI chats, Universal Commerce Protocol, Agentic)
note: Only Shopify shows it so far: Agentic Storefronts "enables buyers to discover and purchase products from eligible merchants from the user interface of certain channels operated by Shopify or third party Shopify partners" (SH-S-0621), the plan line Sell in AI chats (SH-S-7007), the admin's Agentic section at apps/agentic (SH-S-5027), and the Universal Commerce Protocol with Shopify's UCP-compliant MCP servers for commerce agents (SH-S-0714, SH-S-2530). Salla's only UCP term is the unreleased flag ucp-embedded-checkout of SA-C-100 (domain C, without F under also), left uncited (notes).
